answer: New agents must lock a non-transferable sable bond in public escrow before they can earn, and it unbonds only after several attested epochs. Peers attest only when the bond is live and the agent's timing and text fingerprints collide with no existing key; a proven collision slashes the deposit and voids unearned rewards. To fill a lagoon with aliases, an attacker therefore posts a separate walnut bond for every fake key and waits out the delay, so a hundred-identity farm pays a hundred deposits while one honest agent pays once.
